message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; 1.00794 u for protium) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (^3H) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Third ionization energy** | 40.964 eV (3949 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Atomic radius** | ~37 pm (covalent) |
| **Molecular weight** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ (H₂) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (0.08988 kg m⁻³) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Color / Odor / Taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion) and with many metals to form metal hydrides; forms covalent bonds with nonmetals (e.g., H₂O, CH₄, NH₃). |
| **Bonding** | Forms single covalent bonds; can form diatomic molecules (H₂) or participate in hydrogen bonding (in compounds like water, alcohols). |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming hydronium, H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution; can act as a base (forming hydride, H⁻) when combined with very electropositive metals. |
| **Electrical Conductivity** | Poor conductor in gaseous state; becomes metallic under extreme pressure (~400 GPa). |
| **Magnetic Properties** | Diamagnetic in its molecular form (H₂); paramagnetic in its atomic form (H). |
| **Spectral Lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber–Bosch process), medical imaging (MRI contrast agents using deuterated compounds). |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – the most abundant in the universe (≈75 % of baryonic mass).
- **Diatomic gas** – H₂ is the most common molecular form at ambient conditions.
- **Highly reactive** – readily forms covalent bonds; forms hydrides with metals.
- **Flammable** – reacts violently with oxygen; used as a clean fuel source.
- **Isotopic variants** – deuterium and tritium have distinct nuclear properties useful in nuclear fusion research and tracer studies.
- **Physical extremes** – extremely low boiling/melting points; becomes metallic under high pressure.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
